newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CABINET APPROVAL CLIMBS BACK OVER 50 PCT.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CABINET APPROVAL CLIMBS BACK OVER 50 PCT.

text.p: Approval rating of the minority Czech cabinet has risen to over 50 percent in September for the first time since it was appointed in July after inconclusive general elections, an opinion poll relased on Monday showed.

The survey conducted by the state-run IVVM agency six weeks before Senate elections said that the cabinet led by centre-right economist Vaclav Klaus enjoyed the trust of 53 percent of Czechs, up from 48 percent in July and August.
The poll, conducted September 2-9 and sampling 1,461 Czechs aged 15 and over, came before the central-bank imposed forced administration of the country's largest wholly-private bank, Agrobanka a.s..

Klaus' previous cabinet saw its approval rating ranging between 47 and 56 percent in the nine months preceeding June 1 general election in which the three-party coalition lost its majority in the parliament.
A survey released last week by the same agency showed that Klaus' personal popularity dropped to 44 percent from 49 percent in June, the lowest level ever since he became Prime Minister in 1992.
Monday's poll also showed President Vaclav Havel's support rising to 82 percent from 78 percent last month, and the parliament's approval rating edging up one point to 35 percent, month-on-month.
